subject.title: Feature: Granular Discord action gates (split actions.messages into read/edit/delete)

question: Should Discord adopt `actions.messages: boolean | { send?: boolean; read?: boolean; edit?: boolean; delete?: boolean }` with omitted fields inheriting the aggregate default, or use a different permanent permission schema?
rationale: This is a shipped configuration and security boundary: maintainers must choose the canonical shape, inheritance and override precedence, and which adjacent Discord actions belong to each capability before implementation can safely encode policy.

options.title: Adopt granular object form
options.body: Preserve the boolean shorthand, normalize boolean and object inputs into one effective capability set, and document omitted-field inheritance and account precedence.

options.title: Add separate flat gates
options.body: Keep `messages` as the aggregate default and add independently named message send/read/edit/delete overrides with explicit precedence.

options.title: Retain coarse grouping
options.body: Keep the current contract and document Discord-level permission restrictions as the supported destructive-action control.

recommendation.title: Adopt granular object form
recommendation.body: Preserve the boolean shorthand, normalize boolean and object inputs into one effective capability set, and document omitted-field inheritance and account precedence.
